name: Web Search
description: Live web research for Webbee — search the web and read pages into clean Markdown. System capability: available to every chat, no setup.

tools.name: skeleton_refresh_web_search
tools.description: Web Search status — the user's heavy-read policy (ask/always/never_heavy). Web research works with no setup: web_search to find pages, read_url to read them.

tools.name: web_search
tools.description: WEB SEARCH — find pages for a query. FIRST step of any web research: returns candidate cards (url, title, snippet, score) but does NOT read page content. The `snippet` is an LLM-ready excerpt and is OFTEN ENOUGH to answer — read pages only when you need more. Then read just the 2–3 BEST urls (not all results). For 'today'/'latest'/'recent' queries you MUST pass recency_days. Use include_domains to focus a site, category to bias content type. Re-run with new wording if thin.

num_results.description: How many candidate results to return.
num_results.title: Num Results

recency_days.description: Only results published within the last N days. REQUIRED for 'today'/'latest'/'recent' queries — ranking alone is NOT recency-sorted.
recency_days.title: Recency Days

type.description: Search type — leave 'auto' unless you need speed (fast/instant).
type.title: Type

category.description: Bias results toward a content category when the query clearly targets one.
category.title: Category

SearchResultItem.description: One web-search candidate card (facts only — relevance is the LLM's job).
SearchResultItem.title: SearchResultItem

return_schema.description: web_search results — a real EntityList, never a dict wrapper.
return_schema.title: SearchResultList

tools.name: read_url
tools.description: READ ONE web page into clean Markdown — the cheap, default reader; ALWAYS try this before the heavy readers. TOKEN ECONOMY via `mode`: triage with mode='metadata' (~0 tok) or mode='outline' (~100 tok) BEFORE pulling mode='full'; mode='tables' for price/data pages. Each result includes `content_hash` — if you already read identical content this conversation, DON'T re-read it. Also returns `outline` and structured `tables` — use those, don't parse tables out of text. If it errors, read the NEXT candidate. If a page is blocked (JS/bot-protection) or is an Office doc, this returns a note pointing to the TOKEN-HEAVY read_url_rendered / read_document tools: tell the user what you found and ask before spending tokens (unless the policy is 'always').

max_tokens.description: Token budget for the extracted content.
max_tokens.title: Max Tokens

query.description: Optional: focus extraction/truncation on this question.
query.title: Query

mode.description: TOKEN ECONOMY — what to return. full=whole page (expensive); main=prose only; outline=heading tree (~100 tok, 'which section?'); tables=only tables (price/data pages); metadata=no body (~0 tok, 'is it worth reading?'). Triage with metadata/outline FIRST, then full/tables on the winner.
mode.title: Mode

return_schema.description: A page read into clean Markdown + extraction metadata.
return_schema.title: PageContent

tools.name: read_url_rendered
tools.description: ⚠️ TOKEN-HEAVY, on-demand. Read a page in a real headless Chromium browser — for pages the normal read_url could NOT open because they need JavaScript or are behind bot-protection (read_url returned CHALLENGE_BLOCKED / 403 / empty). Slow and consumes many tokens. Use ONLY for an IMPORTANT page AFTER read_url failed, and prefer to ask the user first unless they set the read policy to 'always'. Never use as the first reader — always try read_url first.

max_tokens.description: Token budget for the extracted content.
max_tokens.title: Max Tokens

query.description: Optional: focus extraction/truncation on this question.
query.title: Query

mode.description: TOKEN ECONOMY — what to return. full=whole page (expensive); main=prose only; outline=heading tree (~100 tok, 'which section?'); tables=only tables (price/data pages); metadata=no body (~0 tok, 'is it worth reading?'). Triage with metadata/outline FIRST, then full/tables on the winner.
mode.title: Mode

return_schema.description: A page read into clean Markdown + extraction metadata.
return_schema.title: PageContent

tools.name: read_document
tools.description: ⚠️ TOKEN-HEAVY, on-demand. Read an Office document (.docx / .xlsx / .pptx) at a URL into Markdown. Use ONLY when the url points to such a document (read_url returns UNSUPPORTED_CONTENT_TYPE for these). Large spreadsheets/decks consume many tokens — prefer to ask the user first unless the read policy is 'always'. Not for normal web pages (use read_url) or PDFs (read_url already handles PDF).

max_tokens.description: Token budget for the extracted content.
max_tokens.title: Max Tokens

query.description: Optional: focus extraction/truncation on this question.
query.title: Query

mode.description: TOKEN ECONOMY — what to return. full=whole page (expensive); main=prose only; outline=heading tree (~100 tok, 'which section?'); tables=only tables (price/data pages); metadata=no body (~0 tok, 'is it worth reading?'). Triage with metadata/outline FIRST, then full/tables on the winner.
mode.title: Mode

return_schema.description: A page read into clean Markdown + extraction metadata.
return_schema.title: PageContent

tools.name: set_web_read_policy
tools.description: Set the user's standing policy for the TOKEN-HEAVY web readers (read_url_rendered / read_document). Call when the user expresses a preference: 'читай всегда' / 'always read' / 'don't ask just read' → 'always'; 'не читай тяжёлое' / 'stop reading heavy pages' → 'never_heavy'; 'ask me first' → 'ask'. Persists per-user across sessions.

policy.description: ask=warn+ask before heavy reads (default); always=auto-read blocked/Office pages; never_heavy=never use the heavy readers.
policy.title: Policy

tools.name: capture_page
tools.description: SEE a web page — real screenshot + machine FACTS from a headless Chromium on the api-server (webbee-eyes cloud tier, for panel/Telegram — the terminal uses its local webbee-eyes organ instead). Returns console errors, failed requests, an accessibility role tree (also your click/type targeting map), page meta and, unless with_screenshot=false, a file_id whose screenshot you can READ with file-reader read_files (ai_vision). Optional pre-capture actions (click/type/press/scroll/wait/waitfor/goto/eval) run on the SAME page, so you can log into a form or open a tab before the shot. Use to VERIFY what you built, to check how a page really looks, or to debug layout — never as a text reader (read_url is for content).

viewport.description: Screen shape: desktop 1920x1080, laptop 1366x768, tablet 768x1024, mobile 390x844.
viewport.title: Viewport

full_page.description: True = full scroll-height capture (bigger PNG, slower).
full_page.title: Full Page

wait_ms.description: Extra settle delay before the screenshot (max 10s).
wait_ms.title: Wait Ms

actions.description: Optional pre-screenshot actions on the SAME page, in order — [{type:click|type|press|scroll|wait|waitfor|goto|eval, ...}] — e.g. [{"type":"type","selector":"#email","text":"a@b.c"},{"type":"click","selector":"button"}]. Stops at the first failing action; the log lands in the result.
actions.title: Actions

with_screenshot.description: True: upload the PNG into File Reader (returns file_id; ai_vision reads it back via read_files). False: facts-only (console/network/a11y/meta).
with_screenshot.title: With Screenshot

return_schema.description: A page read into clean Markdown + extraction metadata.
return_schema.title: PageContent

tools.name: read_urls
tools.description: READ SEVERAL web pages in ONE call, concurrently — the bulk form of read_url. Use this whenever you want more than one page (e.g. the top 3 results of a search): it is much faster than calling read_url repeatedly. TOKEN ECONOMY: max_tokens is the budget for the WHOLE batch and is split across the pages, and mode defaults to 'main' (prose only) — use mode='outline' or 'metadata' to triage many candidates cheaply before a full read. Pass `query` to focus every extraction on your actual question. Dead or blocked links are reported per URL and never discard the pages that did read; if an important page comes back blocked, fall back to the single-page read_url for it, which can escalate to the heavy readers.

params_schema.description: Read SEVERAL pages in one call.

urls.description: The pages to read (http/https), up to 10. They are fetched CONCURRENTLY, so this is much faster than calling read_url once per page — always prefer it when you have several candidates from a search.
urls.title: Urls

max_tokens.description: Token budget for the WHOLE batch, split across the URLs — NOT per page. Reading more pages shrinks each page's slice rather than multiplying the total cost.
max_tokens.title: Max Tokens

query.description: Optional: the question you are trying to answer. Extraction is focused on it, which makes each page's smaller slice far more useful. Pass it whenever you have one.
query.title: Query

mode.description: TOKEN ECONOMY — what to return per page. Defaults to 'main' (prose only), which is the right choice for almost every batch. Use 'outline' or 'metadata' to triage many candidates cheaply before a full read of the one that matters; 'full' only for a small batch you genuinely need in full.
mode.title: Mode

params_schema.title: ReadUrlsParams

BulkPageResult.description:
One page's outcome inside a batch.

`outline` and `tables` are carried alongside `content` because the cheap
triage modes return their payload in those keys and leave `content`
empty — dropping them would make mode='outline'/'tables' silently
useless in a batch, which is exactly the mode a multi-URL read wants.
BulkPageResult.title: BulkPageResult

return_schema.description: Combined outcome of a bulk read.
return_schema.title: BulkReadResult
